newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-IOC WELCOME REDUCED DOPING BANS.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-IOC WELCOME REDUCED DOPING BANS.

text.p: Olympic chiefs welcomed on Friday a decision by the world governing athletics body to reduce bans for drug cheats.
On Thursday, the International Amateur Athletic Federation (IAAF) congress voted to halve the ban for serious drugs offences from four to two years.
The decision was criticised by Olympic and world high hurdles champion Allen Johnson and former Olympic and world 100 champion Linford Christie.

But International Olympic Committee (IOC) director general Francois Carrard said it was important that it was possible to enforce bans and added the longer suspension had provided a major legal problem.
"I can understand their (the athletes') concern," Carrard said. "(But) we welcome the step. It is a good move towards harmonisation of sanctions.
"It is not what is put on paper as the term. What is enforceable is the most important thing."
The IAAF has been put in an impossible position after fighting a losing and financially disastrous war with civil courts who have ruled that four-year bans represent unacceptable restraint of trade.
